Solid 6DOF FPS reminiscent of Forsaken and the Descent games, but with procedurally generated levels. The physics and controls are really satisfying, with just the right balance between weight and speed. The levels are kind of abstract looking and seem to be generated based on a large variety of prefabricated modules, but look good and are varied enough that they don't bore you. They serve the purpose of preventing rote memorization as a long term strategy really well. Visually, I'd say the game reminds me of Forsaken most of all, complete with the late 90s blown-up, interpolated, muddy texture and low poly environment aesthetic, Lighting and shading however feels modern. The sound design is great, with sounds that are legible and distinct enough to be informative without being annoying or unsatisfying. The music is good and doesn't get in the way but after a few hours the overwhelmingly positive impression doesn't seem to last for as long as for the other elements of the game. It's not bad, but there maybe just isn't enough of it. As of writing this review, the game is still in early access, but the game is well worth the full price as it is at this point.

6DOF with damn good satisfying gameplay, but leaves more to be desired in level design. Edit: This was the case up until the 0.9.9e patch that dev somehow believed would improve the game, came out. Number of primary weapons that you can carry are reduced from 4 to 3 (and they used to be even more than that in the past too). Not only that, but now you cannot switch into a primary or secondary weapon that you don't have any ammo for, which means you cannot swap them out with something that dropped. How is reduced number of choices and options a good improvement for a 6DOF game is beyond me. You can no longer get extra lives from points, a pointless departure from Descent's tried and approved risk vs. reward system. The drops are calculated according to what you miss the most at the current moment. Sounds right on the paper, but it's completely pointless for the type of game this is, and it actually takes away tactical dimensionality the game used to have. This is a roguelike game, the drops are supposed to be completely random, and thus make you adopt a different approach depending on what you have available on hand, that's the strength of a randomized game. If you are missing shields and all of a sudden all drops are shields, you are just fooling yourself about overcoming difficulty. Nothing but a definitive downgrade, how could a dev think that any of this was a good idea is beyond me. And they have released the game in this sad state. It feels more like a demo than a full game right now. Play two runs and you've basically experienced the entire game. 6DOF games like this make me feel more thankful for games like Descent 2 and Overload despite their own shortcomings.

本测评写就于游戏刚发售时，本评论基于1.00b版本，所以不涉及任何更新争议。 完成度对于这个价格的游戏而言依旧稍显不足，潜力令人期待，但前提是开发组后续会积极更新。但是刨除完成度的问题，依旧是一款有诚意的融入了roguelike元素的类Descent游戏，考虑到这个品类的选择之少，喜欢类Descent的6DOF射击的玩家依旧可以考虑入手。 [h2]复古？还是单纯的粗糙？[/h2] 最劝退我的就是画风，咋说，也就能比Descent好点了，我认为复古至少应当给人积极的视觉享受，在既有的旧画风的基础上深入优化，做不到的话就并非复古风，而是单纯的粗糙了。某些枪管让我觉得自己拿着两把假阳具射击，还有场景看久了眼睛还是比较难受的。敌人也仿佛和背景合在一层，程序生成的关卡设计更加加重了这个问题。 [h2]流程体验和战术深度[/h2] 游戏单局打通也就30min，且关卡间可以保存，实事求是地说，手感很不错。这种游戏只要做好了移动和射击的核心机制，都有点小爽感。虽然关卡因为Roguelike的设计，使用了程序生成，但是总体堆砌感不强，流程体验相对流畅，也有隐藏房间等小巧思，值得表扬。战术深度和可重玩性一般，毕竟不是真正的roguelike为取向制作的游戏。 [h2]音画和美术资产复用问题[/h2] 音画体验原味复古，画面可能有意贴近早年间的 3D 射击游戏，我个人持保留态度，但或许有遗老会很喜欢。敌人换色复用现象比较严重，希望后续能改善。 [b] [u]推荐给：[/u] [/b] 经典6DOF射击游戏的爱好者。 追求流畅操作和爽快战斗体验的玩家。 喜欢碎片化时间游玩的玩家。 [b] [u]不推荐给：[/u] [/b] 注重游戏内容深度和多样性的玩家。 对Roguelike要素期望较高的玩家。 追求高品质美术和体验的玩家。 [quote]关注鉴赏组：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45134494]浮生评测[/url] ←"浮生若梦，一鉴倾心，邀您共赏人间烟火" 加入Steam组：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/LLFLLFF]浮生评测[/url]←“一起追寻'浮生若梦'般的游戏体验” 开始“浮生若梦”鉴赏组的奇幻之旅！[/quote]

[h1]《Desecrators》：就这个高速爽！[/h1] 这是一款风格非常old school的弹幕射击游戏——或者我们换个更加经典的名字，「太空打飞机」，从电子游戏鼻祖级别的《太空侵略者》开始就已经经久不衰。而《Desecrators》最大的区别在于，虽然仍旧是以高速射击+躲避弹幕为玩法核心，但它却是第一视角，这样就要求更高的反应速度、以及对地图空间结构的更高标准。与此同时，这种第一视角的「机体感」非常强烈，十分有萝卜片的味道，尽管本作的画面相当抽象。 美术上的瑕疵雀食是肉眼可见，不过游戏在音乐上却相当带感，可以说抓准了这类游戏的成功关窍：射击固然爽，在劲爆的电子乐中高速射击更爽！所以本作在核心玩法相当简洁（射击、升级机体、继续射击）的基础上，美术也瞎眼可见的贫穷，愣生生斩获了97%的超高好评率，我觉得与它超带感的射击体验是分不开的。再加上空灵的机械音与诡异的红绿色调，玩起来还有那么一丢丢的赛博感——与此同时，本作目前没有中文，英文机械音听上去还不错，但是由于有大量关于武器升级的文本描述，所以还是要求一定的英文水平。 总之，即便现阶段内容有些少，但只要你喜欢弹幕射击那这部作品就绝对值得一试，唯一的缺点可能就是相较内容来说价格有点贵，所以也没啥国区用户，maybe是把外区价格直接移植过来了，只能说悲伤，毕竟两边的购买力根本不一样啊喂！ [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

[b]The 6DOF genre hasn't been forsaken. This game is overloaded with all the classic elements to create the perfect descent into chaotic combat[/b]. Desecrators mixes and matches weapons, enemy types, and environmental hazards from various games. But it also stands on its own with how it balances all of these and spins the formula on its own merit. Here you'll find: [b]Arsenal[/b]: There are primary weapons, separated into kinetic, energy, and biomass ammo types (this doesn't influence damage); secondary weapons, which are missiles with different effects (homing or not, clusters, even a gravity pull); and mines. The last two feature a mini-cam that can be used strategically. Primary weapons can be upgraded directly, getting better stats and even utility effects, like recharging shields through damage, or reducing enemies' ship turning rate. Indirectly, there are ship upgrades that help with survivability, maneuverability, ammo stock or damage, including the secondaries and mines. [b]Enemy types[/b]: There are multiple types of tanks roaming around, some melee-exclusive enemies that attack the hull through the shield, and the rest specialize in using one or another weapon that is also available to you. At the end of the ninth level, there's a gigantic boss to beat, but variants also can be fought in the middle of the campaign if you choose to. Worst of all enemies, however, are the Rivals. These invade during certain missions to hunt you down, having the same capabilities as your ship, including the three types of weaponry, their upgrades, and the ship upgrades. [b]Environments[/b]: The levels can have different "biomes", like ice comets or derelict ships, each with their own soundtracks of ambience and combat, and be prone to feature certain enemy types. There is an awesome inclusion of aquatic sections in levels, complete with the dragged movement. Of course, there is both key-hunting and treasure-hunting through different types of gates that partially or completely block the way, often damaging you, and a myriad of secret walls. Enemies can ambush you during exploration with the use of enemy closets and spawner panels. [b]Peculiarities[/b]: Desecrators work on a sort of roguelike gameplay loop. You have to go through nine levels, getting to the save hub after each one, where there will be a choice of two levels. These are procedurally generated and can present different biomes, objectives, a slight bump in difficulty, and the certainty of Rival invasions. Through exploration you'll find weapons and upgrade points. These are completely lost upon failing the campaign; this is indeed a rogueLIKE, not rogueLITE. There's no meta-progression. Failure is running out of lives. You start with three and can be so lucky to find more, but it's game over once you die with zero lives.

Do not be fooled by "single player campaign". This game has zero story, the store page has more story than the game. It's just one procedurally generated level after the other, with the ability to upgrade in between. Expect a randomiced Descent 1, not a Descent 3. As sad as this is, it still feels good to play.

This game is a hidden gem that speaks to the little girl inside of me who has always been in love with cool spaceships and lasers and ♥♥♥♥ like that. The art style of this game is so appealing to me, I couldn't even fully describe what I love about it so much. The retro sci-fi style and the bright pretty colors from all the lasers whizzing by is eye candy. The atmosphere created by the soundscape and art in tandem is nothing short of immaculate. It perfectly invokes the feeling of barging into a long abandoned station drifting silently in space and making more noise than it's likely heard in ages. Piloting the adorable little pirate pod you're put into feels amazing. It's smooth and responsive, but just floaty enough to remind you that you're in zero-gravity, and can roll back and forth to dodge incoming fire. The guns you can fit it with are beefy, punchy, and often very colorful, with even kinetic bullet-fed hardpoints firing bright glowy projectiles. I absolutely love this. The gameplay loop is addicting. Exploring each new space station and searching each little nook and cranny for goods to plunder feels so rewarding and fun. The gunplay is challenging but so incredibly satisfying, hitscan weapons are a rare sight so you often have to lead your shots and I find it very rewarding to land hits with each of the projectile guns. This goes for the enemies too, most shoot slow projectiles like you do and it's equally challenging and rewarding to dodge them. The entire game just feels so good. I have few criticisms of this game so far, and the ones I do are minor. Although each level is really fun to explore, I often find myself scratching my head trying to find secrets so I can get a perfect raid. Even intended level routes can be easy to miss because I feel they sometimes aren't conveyed well enough. There is also absolutely no tutorialization. Desecrators doesn't hold your hand for even a second, you're thrust nuts first into a big space base full of angry killer robots in a little pod that is, at first, very disorienting, and very quietly nudged to look for loot. Both of these minor gripes of mind go hand-in-hand, because with some subtle guidance it'd be much easier to tell that the protrusions on the wall are actually impeding your progress, or that the little metal cones on the floor are actually crates full of goodies. These problems aren't even something I've been experiencing hugely myself because I've been playing games adjacent to this for years, thus I could get a handle of its controls more easily and have a keener eye for its secrets, but I worry that the lack of guidance could create a hurdle for some new players to overcome before they can fully understand and enjoy the flow of this wonderful game. That being said, I understand that this game kinda lies within a particular niche, and many who come to it will already be familiar with its core mechanics. Final note, I thoroughly appreciate the co-op multiplayer. Sharing this joy with my friends has been a blast. The value as well is great, for the peak that this game is it's dirt cheap. Would recommend to anyone interested in roguelikes, and also anyone who hates roguelikes with a burning passion.

Brainless fun and endlessly replayable: Man I love this game. I don't want a story, I just wanna blow up robots and explore. I usually play on Hazard 3 but sometimes I just want a more Power Fantasy experience. I'm an old school Descent fan and while this has more of a Forsaken look to it with all the colored lighting, it really is it's own thing, and I think it belongs right up there with all the other great 6-DOF games that have come out over the years... not that there are that many. Monster (robot) variety is great and they are all a little different, not just in how they look and sound but how they behave and attack. The new biohazard critters are downright terrifying, especially on Hazard 3 and above. Weapons: Huge variety here, some are much more common to come across than others, and all of them have strengths and weaknesses and I think everyone will have their preferred loadout of primary/secondary and mines! Also if you are having trouble, USE YOUR MINES! They are soooo handy and getting good at placing them and learning how different mines work can make or break a run! Levels: Randomly generated and endlessly replayable. As such the layout of the levels honestly kinda makes no sense from a usability stand point. Like no one would want to work or operate and even though they are called "Abandon tomb" or "Derelict Ship" the name of the map doesn't seem to have much effect to what what the level looks like, with the exception of the Prison Lab as those will have these bio-creatures in them and they are MEAN! I dunno maybe I'm missing something. All that said, I don't care! They are fun to explore, and every time I find a secret I get that dopamine hit! Difficulty: For me Hazard 2 is only mildly challenging. Hazard 3 makes me earn it and hazard 4... Never finished a run. I used to not be able to beat Hazard 3 at all, but now I can. Part of it is just being really careful, think ahead, always check your rear view and backtrack often to make sure you're not being followed. The game messes with you and tries to surprise you! Never ever let your guard down. Also explore, and pay super close attention to the walls, lighting, little sparks and buttons. I flipping love this game. It's a nice escape and just brainless fun. It also has relatively low system requirements but not quite as low as you would think based on the graphics. It also has co-op and that's a blast with higher difficulty and voice comms of some kind. I wish it also did LAN PvP "deathmatch". I also wish the dev would add maybe like a big heavy slow moving ship with lots of shields and armor and a light fast ship with low armor/shields for a more twitchy play style but those are far from "missing features". I can't believe how many hours I've managed to put into this game that has basically zero story. For me.. It's just THAT replayable. Big thanks to the Dev! I love this game!

Mouse input does not work correctly. When using the mouse it is not possible to reach the full turn speed you can achieve with a controller. Increasing sensitivity makes it twitchier at low speed but does not increase maximum speed. I posted a discussion thread about this and they told me to try the beta branch then deleted my thread so I can't reply. So I guess I'll just post here that the beta branch is different but still does not work correctly. The graphics are a bit too N64 for my taste, The projectiles are nice but the world is chunky with mostly brown blurry textures, often stretched out. There are cheap details like the doors that squish open rather than animate. There's a random offset applied to each vertex so the whole level looks like a grade school arts and crafts project that someone sat on. The underwater sections look nice. Randomly assembled levels are hard to navigate and have weird spikes in difficulty. You can go into a tunnel, push a button, and a dozen damage sponge enemies will spawn behind you. Levels have no design sense due to being random, so the handle to open a forcefield can be on the other side of the planet. There's no logic to the texturing, random walls will look like door or secrets but they're just randomly assigned different textures. You constantly have to consult the map because the level design is random. All of the enemy ships are better than mine, in terms of damage output, durability, and manueverability. I have to plink at them from a distance and avoid engaging more than one at a time. I find weapons but can't collect them because I have no slots. It takes 3+ missions worth of points to buy a mediocre upgrade.

Once you've made it to level 9, you've pretty much experienced the game. The weapons feel very unbalanced and the levels are absolute mazes. You *need* to acquire every single secret in every level or you will never have a chance at the last level, which leads to a lot of "dud" runs where you make it to the end only to realize you just don't have the upgrades you needed. Upgrades are random, such as getting 4 pyro upgrades but never receiving a pyro the entire time. All this is to say the game is based too much on randomness for my taste. It may be what others are looking for, but I found this game to be really frustrating when you've invested so much time in a run and then die to a one-shot from around a corner, etc. At least I got it for sale I guess, but I doubt I'll play it again. I also really wish you could disable rivals or at least turn down how twitchy they are.

- completely broken "art direction" to the point where it's impossible to distinguish doors from walls. This is worse than first level design mistakes. Basically, the signaling of the levels is so bad I can only see it as purposely trolling me. I thought I just had to get used to forsaken inspired art style, but no, it's just horrible. - very bad audio cues for enemies/shots. Audio in general is pretty bad. - no explanation on items/mechanics at all, and many things are unnecessarily cryptic (e.g. "resurrector" instead of "extra life" etc.) - random level generation is completely simplistic to the point where it's just broken. large enemies in tiny rooms. Powerful enemies spawning out of thin air directly behind you. - the forsaken style tanks have a certain appeal - I want my money back. (For reference, I played through Descent 1 & 2 on high difficulty settings multiple times.)

Anyone who liked forsaken or Descent should easily enjoy this. Everything is really well done here if you know what to expect. No story whatsoever just pure gameplay that's an omage to forsaken and the n64 graphics style. I like the size of the levels that are never too big so it might get tedious to navigate and speaking of navigation: the game has a small but cool feature that let's you put a waypoint to an unexplored area with the press of a button. So you find a switch somewhere that opens something somewhere else and want to go there? Open the map, press a button, set the waypoint, boom. No stomach ache inducing 360 degree searching needed. I also like the weapon variety. From standard laser and gatling guns to shotgun like, charging, rail gun, homing, sentry, mines, rockets.. you name it. It's a shame that this genre doesn't seem to find a bigger audience. There are only a handful of games like this out there while basically every other genre is flooded with content. Anyway I am enjoying this very much so thank you to the developer. Go and buy this so we might get a chance to some more from this underrated genre!

Definitely worth the money. The two things that stuck out to me were the sound design, and the minimalism. Be guy Have ship Take stuff Blow stuff up in process The sound is crisp, and matches what you are seeing and doing. It feels like the old Win 95 games, but plays and looks way smoother. The music is very "on brand", I would say. Everything that made the old 6DOF games fun has been included, imo. It has been many years since Descent 2 for me, so the 6DOF takes some getting used to, definitely. Not only the controls, but also mentally mapping the level. You can choose how auto-leveling works, if you want it at all. Some other reviews complain about the level design. I won't say they are wrong. But there is a line: how do you create a dark, claustrophobic setting that is also visually varied enough to easily navigate? Should it be easy to navigate? That's an individual choice I would say. But, when you complete a level, there is an oncreen visual guide that leads you out, which definitely matters because sometimes you are on a time limit. Motion sickness can be a risk. If that is something that you struggle with, you might struggle with this game. Just a fair warning - not a criticism by any means. Nature of the beast, and all. The upgrade system is also very simple, but definitely influences gameplay meaningfully. Glad I found this, and great job to the team. Really enjoy.

An extremely fun shooter rougelike that can be tactical or hectic fun. Great with a friend and great for quick solo runs. Highly recommend this game for the price. If they would add even a few new ships you can play as that would be wicked.

Mouse input is not handled well *at all.* I've come to realize this is apparently a preference of Descent-like players, but moving the mouse quickly results in less movement than moving the mouse very slowly, which feels absolutely terrible to me. Controller implementation fares either not much better or worse, depending on your preferences: The joystick *is* actually analog, though you're forgiven for not realizing this. Enable Steam Input, set a custom response curve of 45 and an anti-deadzone of 65000 and it feels mostly alright, though you'll also want to use Steam Input to change your inversion - the in-game setting is reversed on controller and does not save between sessions. You'll also want to rebind left on the D-pad to the left arrow key if you want to navigate menus, as that button just doesn't work unless you do so. Ignoring the outright broken input handling, the game itself is unfortunately just mostly okay, greatly buoyed by its excellent graphics and music, which are highly nostalgic and really hit the mark they're aiming for. Bravo. I love seeing the PS2/OG Xbox aesthetic getting love in the indie space. This also means it runs beautifully, which is appreciated. The auto-roll is surprisingly unobtrusive and really helps with orienting yourself in the labyrinthine stages, and the thing that shows you where to go greatly cuts down on navigational annoyances, which is great. These are two smartly designed and much appreciated systems. Unfortunately, enemies are extremely tanky, combat is incredibly hard to read, and most combat ends up taking place in cramped corridors that leave little room to avoid taking damage from the walls of bullets constantly heading your way. I was debating getting a refund and asked my self "how early access is this game?" And the answer is that it's not. It's still getting updates, but this is in an unacceptably rough - honestly just broken - state for it to be in post-1.0.
